ब्रह्मास्त्र के फैंस के लिए आई है एक बड़ी गुड न्यूज़! 🎬

आईएफएफआई २०२६ के दौरान निर्देशक अयान मुखर्जी ने कंफर्म किया है कि वो Brahmastra 2 पर काम कर रहे हैं।
उन्होंने बताया कि पिछली बार फिल्म में वेस्टर्न इन्फ्लुएंस था, पर इस बार वो इसे और ज़्यादा इंडियन बनाने की कोशिश करेंगे।
अयान ने यह भी माना कि पहले इस फिल्म का नाम Dragon रखने का विचार था।
ओटीटी वर्जन को लेकर उन्होंने कहा कि स्ट्रीमिंग पर मौजूद वर्जन सिनेमा हॉल वाली फिल्म से थोड़ा अलग है।
उनका दावा है कि सिनेमा के लिए उन्होंने फिल्म को तेज़ करने के चक्कर में कुछ सीन काट दिए थे।
अयान के मुताबिक, कभी-कभी ज़्यादा सोचने से चीज़ें बेहतर होने के बजाय खराब हो जाती हैं।
क्या आपको Brahmastra का ओटीटी वाला लंबा वर्जन पसंद आया था या थिएटर वाली फिल्म बेहतर थी? 🔥🤔

ctx.text:
On day 3 of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Brahmastra (2022) director Ayan Mukerji and Minnal Murali director Basil Joseph had a session on 'The Epic Genres – Mythologies, Superheroes & New Worlds'. Ayan confirmed that he's working on Brahmastra 's sequel.
He said, "As we step into Brahmastra 2 , I hope we can make it even more Indian. What happened with me when I began Brahmastra was that there were certain Western influences in mind. There were stories from the West which I enjoyed like Harry Potter , to give you an example. Also, they (Hollywood) dabbled more in this genre in these last 10-15 years. They were doing more superhero and fantasy films. In Brahmastra , there was a touch of Hinduism and Indian spirituality which was a part of the writing. As I started writing, I realized that it's an interesting original stuff that started to call me more and more. That's why, the film was originally called Dragon and it got rechristened to Brahmastra ."
He also revealed that one can enjoy a longer version of Brahmastra on digital. He said, "The film I put out on streaming is a slightly different edit than the one we released in cinema. Because I was watching the film again and again and again, we edited certain scenes in a very sharp way when we put it out in cinemas. Honestly, I had seen those scenes so many times myself that by the time I was watching it for the 500th time, I knew every beat of the scene. So, I was finding the scenes a little bit slow. I thought, 'Let me cut the pauses of the actors. Let me make it go faster and faster'."
He revealed, "To those scenes, I got a very different reaction from the audience when they saw the film as compared to when I had shown the film to a lot of people in the office. That's because the film that they were seeing was a different film than the final version that I had put out. So, that was a note to myself that sometimes, you feel that you are improving something. But overthinking is not always improving."
